scope: Proposition 5.1 (Bounds at integer reference dimensions) of the manuscript “Cylinder loop weights and planar nesting” (preprints/Cylinder-loop-weights-and-planar-nesting-September-26-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 237 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 2e5effc6ded13360), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 52. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix | Re η| ≤ a0 < π and | Im η| ≤ b0 < ∞, with the parameter conventions of Proposition 3.6. For nonnegative integer dimensions νσ, put Lν,j(M) = log |ei(η+πf+2πj)M Fν(M)|, v = Im M. The following estimates hold. 1. If M is real and 0 ≤ νσ ≤ CeγL, then, without any restriction on the explicit counts, Lν,j(M) ≤ ChL + Chne − chde. This bound is independent of the integer alias j. 2. Suppose ne is polynomially bounded, as in part 2 of Proposition 3.6. In the same dimension range, for every real v and integer j, Lν,j(M) ≤ ChL + Chne − chde − 2πjv + Ch(v2 + (1 + f)|v|). (40) 3. Assume the common hypotheses of parts 3 and 4 of Proposition 3.6, polynomial bounds on ne, |j|, |M|, ℓe, and νσ ≍ m. Choose the imaginary imbalance and trial density from part 3 of that proposition. Then Lν,j(M) ≤ ChL + Chne − chde − cδU2 L + o(L). (41) If U ≤ U0, the choice from part 4 instead gives Lν,j(M) ≤ 3γL 8 − 2L Re(η2) 4κ + CεL + o(L) + Chne − ch,εde. (42) Here δ can be taken sufficiently small without degrading the displayed damping and per-particle constants, and U0 may then be fixed arbitrarily, as in part 4 of that proposition. The estimates are uniform once the parameters in the trial bounds and the polynomial size powers are fixed.
